title: cowork-harness critique --output-format json report (and critique-report.json run-dir artifact)
description: EXPERIMENTAL, descriptive schema — NOT a SPEC §12-frozen surface: additive field changes are expected between minor versions (unlike doctor.json). It exists so automation consumers (budget pacers, harvesters) have authoritative field names/shapes instead of prose. Exactly one of infraFailure / evaluatorError / evaluatorModel-with-findings describes the outcome; items is [] on both failure branches.

skillFolder.description: the positional folder BOTH turns mounted (a plain skill, or a plugin root)

outDir.description: the kept run dir (turns/1 = graded, turns/2 = reflection; critique-* artifacts at its root)

fidelity.description: the tier critique pinned for both turns; always concrete (--fidelity cowork is resolved at parse time, never forwarded as-is)

requestedFidelity.description: what the caller asked for when it differs from what ran — present only for --fidelity cowork, naming the tier it resolved to in `fidelity`

gradedEffectiveFidelity.description: best-effort: the tier the graded turn's own result.json RECORDS (should equal fidelity; both surfaced so a mismatch is visible)

gradedBaseline.description: best-effort: the graded turn's fingerprint.baseline (Desktop appVersion)

costUsd.description: per-critique cost across the FOUR model workloads. GATE ON `complete` BEFORE TRUSTING totalUsd: false means one or more workloads were unpriced and the total UNDERCOUNTS true spend.

evaluatorPass1Tokens.description: token split for one evaluator pass. Answers 'is this pass's money evidence or thinking?' — the question that decides whether sending more evidence is cheap. cacheRead is separate because it prices at a tenth of fresh input

evaluatorPass2Tokens.description: token split for one evaluator pass. Answers 'is this pass's money evidence or thinking?' — the question that decides whether sending more evidence is cheap. cacheRead is separate because it prices at a tenth of fresh input

gradedSkill.description: the resolved skills/<name> the packager graded (--skill or single-skill auto-selection); ABSENT for a plain skill folder. Multi-skill-plugin pairing key: skillHash keys the whole mounted plugin, so pair by (gradedSkillHash, gradedSkill), never skillHash alone

skillInvocationObserved.description: advisory: whether an observable channel — the main agent's Skill tool calls, a sub-agent's Skill calls (from the turn's events.jsonl), or a leading staged-skill slash token in the prompt — named gradedSkill; false = every channel was observable and none did (the critique may be grading a run that never invoked the selected skill); ABSENT = a channel could not be observed or the one that fired is ambiguous (see commandShadowsSkill), which is never a synonym for false

commandShadowsSkill.description: advisory: the plugin ships BOTH commands/<gradedSkill>.md and skills/<gradedSkill>/SKILL.md, so the slash entry and the Skill tool launch either through one registry and the run records the name, not the kind — skillInvocationObserved is therefore absent or false, never true; present only when true

referenceAccessUnobservable.description: the graded run recorded no reference-access list (a run kept before the signal existed, or one with no observable tool stream), so noSkillFilesRead is absent and must be read as unknown, never as "nothing was read"; present only when true

gateAnswers.description: the graded run's resolved gate answers, for a deterministic follow-up run

taskResult.description: the graded turn's own result — error is a GRADEABLE outcome, not an instrument failure

gradedOutcome.description: the graded turn's result.json outcome (e.g. delivered_clean)

gradedSkillHash.description: content-exact hash of the MOUNTED folder — the cross-FIX pairing key (per-plugin under --skill)

selfReportStatus.description: unavailable = pass 2 was skipped; findings are pass-1-only

evaluatorIntegrity.description: mechanical canary check per pass; false = that pass ignored a trusted instruction — an empty critique may be adversarial silencing, not a clean skill

droppedEvaluatorItems.description: malformed items the per-item-tolerant parse dropped; non-zero means the surviving findings under-represent the full reply

turn1ResultDegraded.description: the graded turn's canonical result was corrupted/never archived — result-derived sections are empty DEFAULTS, treat as unknown

turn1SliceDegraded.description: the turn-1 transcript slice's boundary could not be trusted — treat gaps as unknown

skillMdStatus.description: readability of the packaged SKILL.md; missing/unreadable force the mechanical already-covered -> not-adjudicable downgrade. untracked = present on the host but NOT delivered by staging (git-tracked files only), so it was never in the agent's mount and is not valid evidence

evidenceBudget.description: what the evaluator was actually shown. Skill-authored content (SKILL.md + references + every dispatchable agent md) ships WHOLE; these fields exist so a consumer never has to read compiled source to learn the budgets — the previous per-file caps were discoverable only by inspecting dist/, and let 11 of 13 reference files go permanently ungraded with no signal

corpusBytes.description: total bytes of skill-authored content found, BEFORE any ceiling cut

corpusCeiling.description: the sanity ceiling governing SKILL.md + references + every dispatchable agent md COMBINED

corpusCuts.description: per-file record of what the ceiling cut. EMPTY on every real skill. omitted:true means the file's share fell below the minimum useful slice — a different instruction to the author (split this file) than a partial cut (the corpus as a whole is too big)

corpusExcluded.description: skill files present on the HOST but excluded because staging would not deliver them (untracked, git-mode on). They were never in the agent's mount, so grading against them would manufacture false already-covered verdicts — but the author must be told, or the grade silently covers less than they believe

corpusPackaged.description: every corpus file whose CONTENT shipped into the corpus sections, by the same key corpusCuts uses. Excludes a file the ceiling zeroed and a placeholder for an unreadable file; a PARTIALLY cut file IS listed, with its loss in corpusCuts. OPTIONAL and deliberately absent from `required`: reports predating the field omit it, and requiring it would invalidate every stored report

corpusOmitted.description: corpus files present but NOT packaged, with the reason — plugin-root references/ files under <plugin>/references/ (a raw HOST walk), plus any resolved sub-agent whose file could not be read (`unreadable`), which would otherwise appear in no field at all. (A raw filesystem walk, so an UNTRACKED file — which staging would not deliver — is listed here too; `alsoUntracked` says so when it was evaluated.) OPTIONAL and deliberately absent from `required`: reports predating the plugin-root reference corpus omit it. A narrow selection rule is only safe if what it leaves out is visible, which is what this field is for

name.description: the file's DISPLAY key (<plugin>/references/<path>) — the same spelling corpusCuts and corpusPackaged use, never the plugin-root-relative accept key

alsoUntracked.description: true when staging would ALSO not deliver this file, so linking it is not enough on its own. THREE-state: ABSENT means trackedness was not evaluated (git mode off, not a work tree, or the tracked set could not be read) — absent is never to be read as false

trimRecord.description: which sections the overall belt-and-suspenders trim shaved and by how much. Replaces a bare boolean that made transcript loss undetectable after the fact

packageTruncated.description: ANY section was cut — most often the transcript's 128 KiB head+tail elision, the cut that actually happens on long runs. This is what adds the evaluator's truncation caveat, so a consumer reading DROPPED findings or a rise in not-adjudicable needs it; corpusCuts is empty in that case and would otherwise imply nothing was cut

verdictProvenance.description: advisory scoping: the verdict is a self-run discovery lead, never an independent attestation

infraFailure.description: instrument failure (task turn killed / reflection protocol broke) — no critique was produced; items is []; process exits 2

evaluatorError.description: the evaluator threw (embeds the raw reply) — no critique was produced; items is []; process exits 2; see critique-salvage.json

evaluatorModel.description: the transport-RESOLVED evaluator model (never the requested alias); present only when the evaluator completed

evaluatorTransport.description: how the evaluator's calls were made: `isolation` (the level of isolation from the operator's own Claude Code setup) the host CLI's `cliVersion`, the `effort` it was called with (absent from a report written before it was recorded), `settingsEnvOverride` (the effort/thinking keys a user-settings `env` block sets, names only, which the call blanks) and `settingsMaxEffort` (a user `maxEffortLevel`, which clamps the effort when below it), and `strictMcp: false` when the call left out `--strict-mcp-config` for an enterprise MCP config; present with evaluatorModel

items.description: the citation-validated findings from both passes. citationResolved:false = the cited excerpt did not resolve verbatim against the evidence package (DROPPED section — transparency only, do not act on as-is)

evidence.description: the model's cited excerpt — verbatim-checked against the evidence package

findingFingerprint.description: sha256/16 over normalized, secret-scrubbed idea+classification+recommendedAction (evidence excluded). Cross-INPUT clustering key — HIGH-PRECISION, LOW-RECALL: idea is model-authored free text, so a MATCH proves the same finding recurred; a MISMATCH does NOT prove non-reproduction (the same finding reworded fingerprints differently)

noSkillFilesRead.description: the graded turn ACCESSED no references/ or scripts/ file at all — neither the main agent nor any sub-agent, through any observed tool channel (Read, Grep, or a Bash command naming the path). OBSERVATIONAL: the predicate matches references/+scripts/ only (never assets/, never SKILL.md), and detection UNDER-APPROXIMATES — a `cd` into the skill dir then a bare relative `cat`, a heredoc body, and a $VAR-built path are invisible — so `true` is weak evidence of non-use, never proof the content went unread. Absent when the turn-1 result was degraded, when the skill ships nothing to read, or when the run recorded no observable tool stream (unknown, not zero).

gradedModels.description: the model ids the GRADED (task) turn actually ran on, read back from its own result.json `models` and filtered of the agent's `<…>`-wrapped locally-fabricated entries. The turns are a SUBPROCESS and inherit no model from the caller; they take --model or COWORK_HARNESS_MODEL (critique refuses with neither), and this is the only field that records which model produced the graded behaviour. Absent when no result.json was readable or it recorded no live id.

infraFailurePhase.description: WHICH turn produced `infraFailure` — `task turn` (the graded run) or `reflection turn` (critique's own protocol turn). Required alongside infraFailure (see the `dependencies` keyword): without it the text report falls back to a default phase and can name the wrong turn.

infraFailureKind.description: the failed turn's own classification of WHY it failed. Either a harness ErrCategory (unanswered | usage | boundary | runtime | internal) when it printed a `fail()` error envelope, or a RunResult.resultErrorKind (usage_limit | transport | agent) when it RAN and reported an errored result (exit 1, top-level error null). Absent = killed, or exited with no envelope at all. DO NOT read a present kind as "the instrument is fine": cli.ts's top-level catch funnels every unexpected throw (Docker down, container start failure, missing staged agent, a harness bug) into `internal`, and LegacyRunDirError into `runtime`. Ordinary/actionable = unanswered, usage, boundary, usage_limit, transport; every other value — including one added after this text — renders as an instrument failure, which is how the text header treats it.

gradedErrorReason.description: why a graded turn that ended in result:"error" errored — its `resultErrorKind` (transport / agent) plus the finer termination source. An errored task turn is a GRADEABLE outcome and the critique still runs, so this is what separates a skill defect from a dropped connection. A task turn that reported usage_limit is not graded: it is a task-turn failure (infraFailureKind usage_limit), with no critique. Absent when the run did not error or recorded no classification.
